overview.summary: Civil engineers design, build and maintain structures and systems such as roads, bridges, buildings, water supply and drainage.
overview.problems: They make sure the things communities depend on are safe, durable and built within budget.
overview.worksWith: Architects, contractors, surveyors, clients, government authorities and construction workers.
overview.workplaces: Design offices and construction sites, with some roles in government, consulting firms and construction companies.

timeline.title: Review drawings and plans
timeline.description: The engineer checks design drawings, quantities and any updates before work starts for the day.
timeline.why: Errors in drawings become expensive and risky once they are built.

timeline.title: Site visit and inspection
timeline.description: The engineer walks the site with the contractor, checks that the work matches the plan, takes measurements and photos, and checks safety arrangements.
timeline.why: Checking real work against the design protects safety and quality.

timeline.title: Coordination meeting
timeline.description: The engineer discusses progress, delays and materials with contractors, suppliers, architects or clients.
timeline.why: Construction involves many teams that must work in the right order.

timeline.title: Quality checks and calculations
timeline.description: The engineer reviews material test results, checks calculations and updates schedules and cost estimates.
timeline.why: Structures must be safe and durable while staying within budget.

timeline.title: Reports and planning for tomorrow
timeline.description: The engineer writes a progress report, records any issues and plans the next day's inspections.
timeline.why: Written records show what was done and help resolve disagreements later.

timeline.title: Solving problems at short notice
timeline.description: Bad weather, a late delivery or unexpected ground conditions can change the plan and call for quick decisions.
timeline.why: Real sites rarely go exactly as planned.

responsibilities: Designing or checking structures so they meet safety codes
Managing safety and compliance on site
challenges: Site work can be outdoors in heat, rain or dust.
Responsibility for public safety is serious, because mistakes can have large consequences.
Delays can come from weather, approvals or supply problems outside your control.
Some projects are far from home and involve travel.
Many countries require professional registration or a licence for senior responsibility.
workEnvironment: A mix of office work for design and calculations and construction sites for inspection and supervision. Some roles are mostly in a design office and others mostly on site. Protective equipment is required on sites.
rewards: Seeing a road, bridge, building or water system you helped create
Variety of projects over a career
A mix of technical and practical work
tradeoffs: Work location can change from project to project
Construction activity can rise and fall with the economy

activity.title: Test which shape holds more weight
steps: Make a small bridge between two stacks of books using a strip of paper or thin cardboard.
Place coins on it one at a time and count how many it holds before bending.
Change one thing, such as folding the paper into a tube or adding a triangle shape, and test again.
Record both results in a small table.
Write what you learned about strength and shape.
activity.outcome: You see why engineers test designs, change one thing at a time and record their results.
activity.safety: Use only light materials and coins, work on a table or the floor, and never test heavy loads or climb on anything.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
